reason: A classification that imposes no requirements on the resulting behavior supplies no deterministic expected runtime outcome. Requiring acceptance, refusal, a crash or a particular value would invent an oracle. Existing explicit diagnostic requirements still need their own tests.

Whether a specification omits a definition is a documentary classification, and undefined behavior permits every resulting outcome. A standalone C# program cannot establish this distinction by requiring one value, diagnostic or execution outcome.

The equivalence of specification indications has no distinct executable outcome: each denotes behavior without requirements. A causal runtime mutation cannot distinguish their emphasis or equivalence without imposing an unsupported restriction.

The old clause permits multiple Unicode editions rather than a fixed character-table revision. A character newly assigned after 3.0 is therefore not a required old refusal, and a successful current compiler probe cannot establish which permitted edition or complete ISO/IEC 10646-1 authority it follows. Concrete character-category and normalization requirements need their own predicates and tests.
